Millimeter-sized single crystals of CaFe1-xCoxAsF were grown using the CaAs flux method.
The chemical compositions and crystal structure of the crystals were characterized carefully.
The c-axis lattice parameter of the undoped crystal CaFeAsF is 8.584 Å.
The c-axis lattice parameter decreases to 8.547 Å with Co substitution.
The superconducting transition temperature (Tc) of the CaFe1-xCoxAsF single crystals is 21 K.
A pressure as small as 0.22 GPa can enhance Tc for about 1 K.
The actual composition of Co in the crystals is x ≈ 0.12.
The composition of the crystals determined by EDS analysis is Ca:(Fe+Co):As ≈ 1:1:1.
The typical crystal size of the grown crystals is 1 mm × 0.7 mm × 0.06 mm.
The temperature dependence of resistivity for the CaFe1-xCoxAsF single crystal with x = 0.12 shows a clear upwarp below 100 K.
The onset of the superconducting transition temperature is about 22 K.
The zero-resistivity temperature is about 20 K.
The magnetic susceptibility of the CaFe1-xCoxAsF single crystal with x = 0.12 shows a high superconducting volume fraction.
The pressure dependence of Tc for the CaFe1-xCoxAsF single crystal with x = 0.12 is studied.
The Tc of the CaFe1-xCoxAsF single crystal with x = 0.12 rises steeply initially and then becomes smooth and stable around a maximum value of 21.5 K.
The CaAs flux method is a self-flux method used to grow single crystals of CaFe1-xCoxAsF.
